_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Translating messy business requirements, stakeholder language, and early product ideas into an implementation-neutral…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "a stakeholder says users place orders that ship in multiple boxes -- how do I capture this as a model before naming tables?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the conceptual-modeling skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is conceptual-modeling the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes conceptual-modeling as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against taxonomy-design, entity-relationship-modeling, entity-relationship-modeling
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the conceptual-modeling workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore conceptual-modeling
Does not route to taxonomy-design, entity-relationship-modeling, entity-relationship-modeling when the conceptual-modeling scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
